faqs.q: How do I choose bridal accessories to match my dress?
faqs.a: Start with the neckline and how detailed the dress is. A high or detailed neckline usually needs no necklace, while a simple strapless dress can carry a statement piece.

faqs.q: Should I wear a veil or a headpiece?
faqs.a: It depends on your hair and style. Hair worn up suits a comb or veil set at the back, while a hair vine or floral piece suits hair worn down or half up.

faqs.q: How does this bridal accessories quiz choose a look?
faqs.a: The final question about wedding style routes the bride to one of four coordinated looks, and the earlier answers help your stylist refine them.

endings.title: Classic and timeless 🕊️
endings.bodyMd: Pearl or diamond-style studs, a fine necklace or none if your neckline is high, and a fingertip or cathedral veil. Classic pieces photograph well and still look right when you look back at the pictures years later.

endings.title: Soft and romantic 🌿
endings.bodyMd: A hair vine or floral comb, delicate gold drops and a soft, simple veil, or no veil at all. Loose, natural pieces suit flowing dresses and look lovely with hair worn down or half up.

endings.title: Clean and modern 🤍
endings.bodyMd: One strong piece instead of many: sculptural earrings or a sleek bow, with a raw-edge or single-layer veil if you want one. A simple dress lets a single statement accessory stand out.

endings.title: Full glamour ✨
endings.bodyMd: Crystal earrings, a sparkling headpiece and a long veil with a beaded or lace edge. If your dress already has a lot of sparkle, pick one of these to shine and keep the rest quiet.
